description.text:
If your footage changes brightness over time, either gradually or suddenly, 
this option will do some extra pre-filtering to help compensate for the changes. 
Enabling this will make the track slower, and may not be as accurate so it should 
only be selected if you know you have to handle changes in luminance.

The blending mode defines how this shape or paint stroke (A) is merged with the elements below it in the stack that have already been rendered (B).
  • color-burn: darken B towards A
  • color-dodge: brighten B towards A
  • difference: abs(A-B)
  • exclusion: A+B-2AB
  • from: B-A
  • hard-light: multiply if A<.5, screen if A>.5
  • max (lighten): max(A,B)
  • min (darken): min(A,B))
  • minus: A-B
  • multiply: AB, A if A<0 and B<0
  • over: A over B
  • overlay: multiply if B<.5, screen if B>.5
  • plus: A+B
  • screen: A+B-AB if A and B between 0-1, else A if A>B else B
  • soft-light: not as extreme as hard-light
Hardness defines the rate of fall off from the brush center to its edge.
Diameter of the paint brush profile, measured in pixels. Shift+drag in the Viewer to set interactively.

Source color for filling the shape or painting the stroke:
  • color: the chosen solid color
  • foreground: the painted result at this point in the hierarchy
  • background: the original unpainted background input
  • background1,2,3: additional image inputs
Spacing between paint brush stamps along the paint stroke.

Specify the paint brush type:
  • paint: solid using the chosen color or paint stroke source
  • smear: displace and blend in the direction of the paint brush
  • blur: blur the area under the paint stroke (use the effect parameter to control the amount of blur)
  • sharpen: sharpen the area under the paint stroke (use the effect parameter to control the radius of sharpening)
If enabled, the paint stroke builds up when painted over itself.
Center of rotation and scaling. To move use Ctrl+drag.
Always pan viewer so the planar surface is centred in the viewer.
Image channels to track

Clamps the tracking patch pixel values to lie between 0 and 1. 
Note: if you want to track using the full dynamic range of your super-white or sub-zero footage, disable this option.
Clear all tracking information.
Clear all tracking information backward of current frame.
Clear all tracking information forward of current frame.

Restrict the output image to a box.
Either the incoming bounding box, the incoming format area,
or the union (combination) or intersection of them.
Color of the shape or paint stroke.
Set the threshold for consistent track generation. Increase the threshold to ensure track motion is locally consistent. Use consistency to prevent poor tracks in complex sequences.
Enable manipulation of the planar surface.
Correction
Use this menu to quickly select between various PlanarTracker layers, or to create a new track layer.
Create the node specified in the menu.

ptracker = nuke.thisNode() 
x = ptracker.xpos() 
y = ptracker.ypos() 
w = ptracker.screenWidth() 
h = ptracker.screenHeight() 
m = int(x + w/2) 
numviews = len( nuke.views() ) 
pt1KnobName = ptracker.knob("pt1").fullyQualifiedName()

ptracker = nuke.thisNode() 
pin = nuke.nodes.CornerPin2D() 
x = ptracker.xpos() 
y = ptracker.ypos() 
w = ptracker.screenWidth() 
h = ptracker.screenHeight() 
m = int(x + w/2) 
numviews = len( nuke.views() ) 

connectNode = None 
try: 
  connectNode = ptracker.input(0) 
except: 
  pass 
try: 
  connectNode = nuke.selectedNode() 
except: 
  pass 

if not connectNode == None: 
  pin.setInput(0,connectNode) 
  pin.setXYpos(m + 2*w, y + w) 

  width = connectNode.width() 
  height = connectNode.height() 

  inKnobs = ["pt1", "pt2", "pt3", "pt4"] 
  outKnobs = ["to1", "to2", "to3", "to4"] 
  for i in range(len(inKnobs)): 
    k = ptracker[inKnobs[i]] 
    p = pin[outKnobs[i]] 
    p.setAnimated(0) 
    p.setAnimated(1) 
    for Idx in range(k.getNumKeys()): 
      t = k.getKeyTime(Idx) 
      p.setValueAt(k.getValueAt(t,0), t, 0) 
      p.setValueAt(k.getValueAt(t,1), t, 1) 

  pin.knob("from1").setValue(0,0) 
  pin.knob("from1").setValue(0,1) 
  pin.knob("from2").setValue(width,0) 
  pin.knob("from2").setValue(0,1) 
  pin.knob("from3").setValue(width,0) 
  pin.knob("from3").setValue(height,1) 
  pin.knob("from4").setValue(0,0) 
  pin.knob("from4").setValue(height,1) 
  pin["label"].setValue("absolute, baked")

description.text:
Create various nodes from the track data,

Use CornerPin2D relative to warp the image according to the relative transform between the current frame and the reference frame.

Use CornerPin2D absolute to set the to position knobs to the corners of the planar surface, and the from knob positions to the dimensions of the currently selected node. This will place the incoming image entirely inside the planar surface. Note: this creates an expression link with the PlanarTracker node, rather than the Roto(Paint) node.

Use CornerPin2D stabilize to apply the inverse transform of the track to stabilize the image. If the PlanarTracker node has not been deleted, this stabilize will attempt to connect to it. This is very useful for making drift corrections. Use Tracker to create a four-corner Tracker node with each of the trackers taking the positions of planar surface corners. This allows you to use the Tracker's transform functions to stabilize, reduce jitter, etc. This export option needs to be baked out in order for the transform to work correctly.

Each of the exports also has a "bake" option, which will copy the values of the key-frames out, instead of creating expression links.

default.value:
ptracker = nuke.thisNode() 
x = ptracker.xpos() 
y = ptracker.ypos() 
w = ptracker.screenWidth() 
h = ptracker.screenHeight() 
m = int(x + w/2) 
numviews = len( nuke.views() ) 
refFrameKnobName = ptracker.knob("reference_frame").fullyQualifiedName() 
pt1KnobName = ptracker.knob("pt1").fullyQualifiedName() 
pt2KnobName = ptracker.knob("pt2").fullyQualifiedName() 
pt3KnobName = ptracker.knob("pt3").fullyQualifiedName() 
pt4KnobName = ptracker.knob("pt4").fullyQualifiedName() 

pin =  nuke.nodes.CornerPin2D() 
pin.setInput(0,None) 
pin.setXYpos(m + 2*w, y + w) 

pin.knob("from1").setExpression(pt1KnobName+'(ref_frame)') 
pin.knob("from2").setExpression(pt2KnobName+'(ref_frame)') 
pin.knob("from3").setExpression(pt3KnobName+'(ref_frame)') 
pin.knob("from4").setExpression(pt4KnobName+'(ref_frame)') 

pin.knob("to1").setExpression(pt1KnobName) 
pin.knob("to2").setExpression(pt2KnobName) 
pin.knob("to3").setExpression(pt3KnobName) 
pin.knob("to4").setExpression(pt4KnobName) 
pin.knob("label").setValue("relative") 

tabKnob = nuke.Tab_Knob('tracking', 'Tracking') 
refFrameKnob = nuke.Int_Knob('ref_frame', 'reference frame') 
refFrameKnob.setExpression(refFrameKnobName) 
setRefFrameScript = "nuke.thisNode()['ref_frame'].clearAnimated()\nnuke.thisNode()['ref_frame'].setValue(nuke.frame())" 
setRefFrameKnob = nuke.PyScript_Knob('set_ref_frame', 'set to current frame', setRefFrameScript) 

pin.addKnob(tabKnob) 
pin.addKnob(refFrameKnob) 
pin.addKnob(setRefFrameKnob)

This is how long the shutter should be open for when motion blurring. The value is in frames, so 0.5 is half a frame.

If the shutteroffset parameter is set to 'custom', this parameter is used to set the time that the shutter opens by adding it to the current frame.

Values are in frames, so -0.5 would open the shutter half a frame before the current frame.

The value of this controls how the shutter behaves with respect to the current frame value. It has four options
  • centred - centres the shutter around the frame, ie: open from f - shutter/2 to f + shutter/2
  • start - opens the shutter starting at the frame, ie: open from f to f + shutter
  • end - closes the shutter at the frame, ie: open from f - shutter to f
  • custom - opens the shutter at the time specified by the shuttercustomoffset parameter.

  else:

    n['track_helper'].setValue(1, 3)

Whether the shape, paint stroke or group is visible and rendered or not.

The 'write on' knobs define how much of the stroke will be rendered at the current frame, with 0 being the start of the stroke and 1 the end. For instance, to do a 'write on' effect, create a stroke that exists over multiple frames and animate the 'end' knob between 0 and 1 so that each frame shows incrementally more of the stroke.

description.text:
The toolbar on the left side of the Viewer includes selection, manipulation, and creation tools. Options related to the current tool appear in a toolbar along the top of the Viewer. Existing shapes and paint strokes can be edited in the node control panel by selecting an item (or items) from the list or in the Viewer. Click on a toolbar item to cycle through the available options for that class of tools. Click and hold or right-click on a toolbar button to open that submenu and select any of its available tool types.

Roto Shapes

Creation

To create a roto shape, select a spline tool and click in the Viewer to place points. You can drag while clicked down to pull out Bezier handles or adjust B-Spline tension as you create the shape. To finish creating the shape and close it, click on the first point or press the enter key. To finish but leave the shape open, press the ESC key.

Soft Edge

To pull out the soft edge, drag on the small line perpendicular to the spline at that point or Ctrl+drag from the point.
If the 'feather lock' option is set, dragging on a control point will move both it and its corresponding soft edge point, otherwise they move independently. Ctrl+drag on a main edge point to temporarily invert the current 'feather link' setting.
Press 'E' to increase the feather point distance on the selected points.
Press Shift+'E' to reset the selected points' feather points to the main point positions.

Bezier

Shift+drag on a tangent handle to snap the opposite handle to the same length.
Ctrl+drag on a tangent handle to move it independently of its opposite handle.

B-Spline

Shift+Ctrl+drag on a point to adjust its tension.The tension is weighted with a power function of 4.

Paint

Shift+click and drag to set the brush size.

Clone Offset

Ctrl+click and drag to adjust the clone source offset relative to its current position.
Ctrl+Shift+click and drag to reset the clone source offset.

Clone Source

Select the Background as source to clone from the primary input. Select Foreground to clone from the currently accumulated result. Note that cloning from the Foreground can cause slower renders. In this case, the order each stroke is rendered matters, so strokes must be rendered sequentially and rendering can't be optimized as it can be when cloning directly from an input image.
Press the 'T' key to toggle visibility of the source onion-skin overlay and source transform handles.

All Splines

Ctrl+Alt+click on the spline to add a point.
Press 'Z' to increase smoothness at a point and Shift+'Z' to cusp it.
Press the Delete key to delete a point.

Transform Jack/Box

Ctrl+drag on an edge to skew.
Ctrl+drag on the center point to move it independent of the selection.
Ctrl+rotate to rotate the jack without moving points.
Shift+drag on the jack or box will disable snapping.
